defects: MAJOR desktop.py:641-642 (_begin_ask): held_keys excludes 0xA5/0x12, so a held Right Alt or generic Alt is never released before the injected Ctrl+C. The target receives Ctrl+Alt+C. Measured with ask combo Alt+F23 (generic Alt, LeftAlt physically held): the Tk target saw keysym c with state 0x2000c (Alt bit) and alt_down=true. Tk tolerates the extra modifier and still copied, but a standard Win32 EDIT control did not copy, so foreground_context returned selection="" (probe e2). With LeftAlt+F23, 0xA4 is not excluded: LeftAlt was released with MARKER, the target saw Ctrl+C state 0xc, and the selection was captured on both targets (s2, e1). The default RightAlt+Space hits the failing branch for every user who is not running Typeless. Fix: release every held modifier that belongs to a configured combo, Alt included, with the same call the T10 paste path uses: release_held_modifiers(keys=self.ptt.relevant_keys()). It sends a MARKER key-up after a NOOP for Alt; the hook skips MARKER events, so the state machine still treats the key as held. The "never inject Right Alt" rule is a test-environment constraint (Typeless). The product paste path already sends a MARKER key-up for Right Alt.

MAJOR desktop.py:30-31 (DEFAULT_HOTKEYS ask = RightAlt+Space; set by the plan). Alt+Space reaches the target unswallowed because the hook never consumes keys. DefWindowProc opens the target window's system menu (#32768) on the Space key-down. The injected Ctrl+C then goes to the menu, so the selection is never captured. For Alt+Space the menu was still open after the session ended, so a later Ctrl+V paste would also land in the menu. Reproduced with LeftAlt+Space and Alt+Space against a Tk Entry (s1, s4: system_menu_seen=true, selection "") and against a standard EDIT control (e3). Fix (planner decision): pick a default ask combo that does not include Alt+Space; or let the hook consume the non-modifier key-down/up only when it completes a configured combo that contains Alt; or cancel the menu (Esc/WM_CANCELMODE) before Ctrl+C. Warn in the hotkey UI when the user sets Alt+Space.

MAJOR desktop.py:1148-1188 (_flush_pastes/_paste): consecutive deferred pastes write the clipboard and fire asynchronous keybd_event Ctrl+V in one synchronous loop. The target reads the clipboard later, so segments are lost or duplicated. Measured on a separate-process Tk Entry with three segments, expected "SEG-ONE SEG-TWO SEG-THREE". Run 1 got "SEG-TWO SEG-THREE"; run 2 got "SEG-ONE SEG-THREESEG-THREE". Hold-to-talk longer than one 8 s chunk queues several segments while the key is held and flushes them together on release. T17 made hotkey paste-back default on, so this is now the default path. The T10 loop had the same pattern, but T17 rewrote this path. Fix: concatenate all pending texts for the same target, then do one clipboard write and one Ctrl+V; or space the pastes out with after() (for example 250 ms apart) and schedule the restore after the last one.

MINOR desktop.py:838-844 vs 883: an ask with no LLM correctly does not paste back. But the warning "沒有可用的 LLM，顯示原始轉錄" only appears inside the per-segment status line, and _poll overwrites it with "已完成。內容已儲存於本機歷史紀錄。" when draining finishes (probe s1 final status). The raw question is also stored as an "ask" history row that looks like an answer. Fix: set session_error (or a persistent note) when mode=="ask" and backend=="Whisper".

MINOR desktop.py:662-663 (_session_context): with "依前景 App 調整格式（傳送視窗標題與 App 名稱給 LLM）" turned off, ask still sends the window title and app name to the LLM chain, including cloud backups. zh/en/translate correctly send none (check_wave_d context_aware_off). Fix: when the setting is off, strip app/title from the ask context and keep only the selection, or say so in the UI.
NIT theme.py:122-157: the Combobox popdown listbox (option_add "*TCombobox*Listbox.*") and the ttk scrollbars are not themed. Screenshots of dark mode and of dark->light show no other leftovers.

The FAIL comes from adversarial real-machine checks: ask selection capture fails with the default Alt-based combo (D1: Alt not released; D2: Alt+Space opens the target system menu), and consecutive pastes garble text (D3).
